The war in Sudan has increasingly relied on drones as it nears its fourth year, with recent fighting concentrated in the southern Kordofan region. Both the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces are deploying surveillance and strike drones, blurring traditional frontlines and expanding attacks beyond military targets. Schools, hospitals and civilian infrastructure have been struck, with the United Nations reporting more than 200 drone-related deaths this month alone and over 500 since January. The shift from urban warfare in Khartoum to drone-enabled strikes across western and southern regions has left civilians increasingly vulnerable.

Al Jazeera's Hiba Morgan reports from Khartoum.

Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq have vowed retaliation against US and Israeli targets amid the wider war involving Iran.

Al Jazeera’s Mahmoud Abdelwahed reports from Baghdad, Iraq.

description:
South Africa's fruit exporters are facing mounting losses and disruption as the US-Israel war on Iran enters its fourth week, threatening a $1.3 billion market in the Middle East. 
Around 90 percent of fruit shipped to the region has been affected, with the Jebel Ali port in the UAE temporarily suspending services after attacks. 
Shipping lines have stopped taking bookings, leaving produce stranded at sea or piling up in South African warehouses, whilst transport costs have surged due to oil supply restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz. 
Exporters are attempting to divert shipments to India, Oman and Sri Lanka, but differing regulatory requirements and limited local market capacity are compounding the crisis as the citrus harvest season approaches.

Al Jazeera's Fahmida Miller reports from Cape Town, South Africa.

Cargo that once moved through key maritime routes in the Gulf is now being rerouted overland through Syria and Jordan. Truck drivers and freight operators say border crossings are busier than they have been in years.

A new emergency agreement between Syria and Jordan has allowed freight crossings to operate 24 hours a day, helping move goods from ports such as Port of Jeddah in Saudi Arabia and Port of Aqaba in Jordan.

From there, shipments travel across the region toward Lebanon, Türkiye, and even into European markets.

Truck drivers say border queues that once lasted hours are now stretching into days as companies race to keep supply chains moving amid the disruption.
